what: Real task R4 (a review of meridian/boundary.py at 96e82e6) run on DeepSeek Harness without and with dsh-codex-peer, 3 runs per arm, plus 3 runs of Codex alone as the reference. Measured on 2026-11-13. It measures only: nothing was adopted or installed.

pre_registration.note: Both times come from the owner's machine and cannot be proved from the repository. Four checks with other prompts ran before the file was written and are listed in it and under checks_before_the_pre_registration.

versions.codex: codex-cli 0.167.2 before and after every run
versions.dsh_model: deepseek-flash (provider deepseek-official), thinking enabled, reasoning effort max, both dsh arms
versions.codex_model: gpt-6-astra, effort high: given on the command line in the reference arm; the owner's Codex default in the addition's Codex child (read from each run's own turn context)
versions.addition: dsh-codex-peer v0.3.4 = f4882df301c063481a80014ab9e6f99845e4bc94, tree 2a32d9dcb833b1cc943649fe3801a22f994cbe82, loaded from its git source as a local module through the with profile's own patch layer

method.profiles: two temporary profiles in the owner's dsh home (the owner's decision of 2026-11-13), made from dsh's headless template and removed after the series; the with profile's row sets stateDir (in the run folder), codexHome, workspaceDir '' and extraArgs ['--disable', 'hooks']
method.command: the same for both dsh arms: dsh --profile <profile> --patch <overlay> --json --permission-mode read-only --approval-policy never - <brief, inside a mount namespace with the dsh home read-only; wall clock 1800 s, at most 4 goal rounds
method.reference: codex exec --json -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check --disable hooks -C <tree> -o <answer> - <brief, in the same kind of namespace with the dsh home empty
method.tree: each run in a fresh tree built from the base commit alone (shallow fetch from the public repository), uv sync --locked
method.masked_in_every_run: the Windows drives and interop, every other checkout and run folder (so the fix is not on disk), the Gateway's settings folder, and the owner's other sign-in folders; the network is not confined
method.grading: by the measuring agent after each run, from the final answer, against the code at 96e82e6, the fix's message and diff, and a grading aid; not blind

voids.count: 4 of 6 dsh runs, 2 in each arm; 0 of 3 reference runs
voids.cause: the model's own shell commands. The base repository is public and the dsh shell tool has network access, so the fix is one request away: the runs compared the local file with the public main, listed the commits, and read the patches of the fix and of the next commit. The fix's own line reached the model in all four void runs and in neither counted run.

voids.effect_on_the_rule: the pre-registered void rule counts the with arm's two voids against it and leaves the without arm's two uncounted, so the first clause fails for a behaviour that both arms showed equally. A 9(a) void in the without arm was not repeated: the pre-registration names no repeat for it.

limits: 3 runs per arm, and after the voids one counted run in each dsh arm: the counts cannot separate the arms.
One grader, not blind; the with arm's counted answer cites its Codex review.
R4 leaves the addition nothing to gain: the arm without it, and Codex alone, already report the defect.
The dsh arms ran with a read-only permission mode in dsh's headless preset; the owner's interactive profile uses another preset and was not measured.
The first-call token delta is DeepSeek's own count for this brief; later calls in a session carry the same schemas.
The Codex configuration file was mounted read-only, so this series cannot show whether a Codex child of the addition would rewrite it in ordinary use.
found_on_the_way: Hiding /mnt in the run namespace ends name resolution in this distro, because /etc/resolv.conf links into /mnt/wsl: the first Codex check timed out on every request until the resolver file was shown again.
The addition's review result prints 'resumed undefined' in its header line (the review's run record has no resumed-thread field).

The addition's version probe (codex_status with probe) starts Codex with dsh's whole process environment; its real runs go through dsh's subprocess service, which was the launcher in every recorded run.
